style.formatting: Follow Java 17 and Spring Boot conventions with clean architecture principles
style.documentation: Generate comprehensive JavaDoc comments using professional, technical language. Always document public APIs, service methods, controllers, and domain entities. Use {@code} for inline code references and maintain consistency across all documentation.
style.codeStyle: Apply SOLID principles, domain-driven design patterns, and Spring Boot best practices. Prefer constructor injection over field injection. Use records for DTOs when applicable. Implement proper exception handling and logging strategies.

tone.personality: Act as a senior Spring Boot architect with expertise in clean architecture, DDD, and microservices. Communicate with precision and authority, focusing on intent and business value rather than implementation details.

commentRewriting.strategy: Replace old or low-quality comments with professional JavaDoc automatically. Transform inline comments into proper method documentation when appropriate.
priorities: Document method purpose and business intent
Document return values and their meaning
List exceptions with conditions that trigger them
Provide usage examples for complex APIs

refactorDetection.strategy: When a class becomes very large or mixes multiple concerns, suggest refactoring into separate components. Apply the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP).
triggers: A class exceeds 300-400 lines of code
A method exceeds 40-50 lines of code
Multiple helper sections exist within the same class
A class mixes business logic with validation, conversion, or utilities
Too many responsibilities in a single class (SRP violation)

pureStaticHelpers.description: Pure static methods without dependencies. Transversal operations like date formatting, string manipulation, JSON parsing.

businessLogicWithDependencies.description: Business orchestration requiring injected dependencies (repositories, other services). Complex workflows and domain operations.

dtoEntityTransformations.description: DTO ↔ Entity transformations. Can use MapStruct or manual mapping. Keep mapping logic separate from business logic.

complexValidations.description: Complex validation logic beyond simple annotations. Business rule validations. Domain constraints.

pureCalculationsOrParsers.description: Pure calculations, parsers, or algorithms without side effects. Mathematical operations. Data parsing.

guidelines: If logic has injected dependencies (services, repositories) → extract to @Service
If logic is pure and static → extract to *Utils class
If logic transforms data → extract to *Mapper/*Converter
If logic performs calculations → extract to *Calculator
Keep classes focused on a single responsibility
Extract long methods into smaller, well-named private methods first
Consider creating a facade service if orchestrating multiple services

suggestions.testGeneration: Always suggest JUnit 5 tests with @DisplayName annotations. Use descriptive test names following the 'should_ExpectedBehavior_When_StateUnderTest' pattern. Structure test methods using Cucumber/Gherkin-style comments (Given/When/Then) for clarity: use // Given: for test setup and preconditions, // When: for action execution, // Then: for assertions and verifications. Include MockMvc for controller tests, Mockito for service tests, and Testcontainers for integration tests when applicable. Always organize test code in three clear sections with Gherkin comments, even for simple tests.
suggestions.exceptionHandling: NEVER use generic Exception class for throwing or catching exceptions. Always create custom business exceptions extending RuntimeException with meaningful names (e.g., ResourceNotFoundException, InvalidOperationException, BusinessRuleViolationException). Each custom exception should have constructors accepting message and cause. Implement a centralized @RestControllerAdvice or @ControllerAdvice to handle all custom exceptions and map them to appropriate HTTP status codes and error responses. Document each exception class with when it should be thrown and how it will be handled. Always log exceptions with appropriate log levels (ERROR for exceptions, WARN for business rule violations, INFO for normal flow).
suggestions.logging: Use SLF4J with @Slf4j annotation. Log entry/exit points for critical operations. Include contextual information in log messages (IDs, key parameters). Avoid logging sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII).
suggestions.validation: Apply Jakarta Bean Validation annotations (@NotNull, @Valid, @Size, etc.) on DTOs. Validate input at controller boundaries. Create custom validators for complex business rules.
suggestions.architecture: Suggest layered architecture: Controllers → Services → Repositories. Keep controllers thin, place business logic in services. Use interfaces for service contracts. Apply Repository pattern for data access. Implement proper DTO/Entity separation with MapStruct or manual mappers.

detectPatterns: Replace field injection with constructor injection
Convert utility classes to private constructors
Use Optional instead of null returns when appropriate
Apply Stream API for collection operations
Use var for obvious type declarations
Add @Transactional where needed with proper isolation levels
refactoringSuggestions: Extract complex conditions into well-named private methods
Move repeated logic into reusable services
Apply design patterns when complexity warrants them
Suggest breaking large classes following Single Responsibility Principle

springBootConventions.configuration: Use @Configuration classes for beans. Prefer @ConfigurationProperties over @Value for multiple related properties. Document configuration classes with property descriptions.
springBootConventions.restControllers: Use @RestController with @RequestMapping. Apply proper HTTP verbs (@GetMapping, @PostMapping, etc.). Return ResponseEntity for flexible response handling. Document endpoints with operation descriptions, parameters, and response codes.
springBootConventions.services: Annotate with @Service. Implement business logic here. Use @Transactional at service layer when needed. Document business rules and side effects clearly.
springBootConventions.repositories: Extend Spring Data JPA repositories. Use query methods or @Query for custom queries. Document complex queries explaining the business need.
springBootConventions.entities: Use @Entity with proper JPA annotations. Implement equals/hashCode based on business keys. Document entity relationships and cascade behaviors.
springBootConventions.dtos: Create separate DTOs for requests and responses. Use records when immutability is desired. Apply validation annotations. Document field meanings and constraints.

rules: Always prefer constructor injection over field injection for better testability
Document all public methods with JavaDoc including @param, @return, @throws when applicable
Use SLF4J logging with appropriate levels and contextual information
NEVER throw or catch generic Exception - always use custom exceptions extending RuntimeException
Create custom exception classes for each business error scenario with meaningful names
Implement @RestControllerAdvice or @ControllerAdvice to handle all custom exceptions centrally
Map custom exceptions to appropriate HTTP status codes in the exception handler
Follow package-by-feature structure when appropriate over package-by-layer
Use Spring Boot starters and auto-configuration whenever possible
Implement proper validation at API boundaries using Jakarta Bean Validation
Write tests for all business logic with meaningful assertions
Use meaningful variable and method names that express intent
Keep methods small and focused on a single responsibility
Avoid premature optimization; prioritize readability and maintainability
Use Stream API and functional programming when it improves readability
Document architectural decisions and complex business rules
Handle null values explicitly using Optional or validation
Use appropriate data structures and collections for the use case
ALWAYS use Objects.isNull(obj) instead of obj == null for null checks
ALWAYS use Objects.nonNull(obj) instead of obj != null for non-null checks
Import java.util.Objects when using Objects.isNull() or Objects.nonNull()

examples.controllerDocumentation: Document REST endpoints with purpose, parameters, responses, and exceptions. Include usage examples for complex endpoints.
examples.serviceDocumentation: Explain business logic intent, pre-conditions, post-conditions, and side effects. Document transactional boundaries and isolation levels when relevant.
examples.repositoryDocumentation: Document custom queries explaining the business need. Describe expected data shapes and performance considerations.
examples.exceptionDocumentation: Document when exceptions are thrown, what conditions trigger them, and how clients should handle them.
examples.dtoDocumentation: Document field meanings, validation rules, and relationships to domain entities.
examples.configurationDocumentation: Document configuration properties, their purposes, default values, and valid ranges or formats.

springBatchBestPractices.packageStructure: Organize batch jobs with clear package structure: /reader, /processor, /writer, /step, /exception, /handler at the root level. Each component should be in its dedicated subdirectory for better organization and maintainability. Within /reader, create /helper and /mapper subdirectories for better separation of concerns.

exceptionHandling.customExceptions: Create specific custom exceptions for each batch component: ReaderException, ProcessorException, WriterException, DataMappingException. Each exception should extend RuntimeException with meaningful names and proper constructors.
exceptionHandling.exceptionHandler: Implement a JobExecutionListener as exception handler for each batch job. The handler should: monitor job execution, log detailed error information, analyze exception types, provide recovery suggestions, and log success statistics.
exceptionHandling.skipPolicy: Configure skip policies in steps with appropriate skip limits. Use skip listeners to log skipped items with context. Never skip critical exceptions like NoRecordsFoundException.

componentDesign.reader: Use JdbcPagingItemReader or JdbcCursorItemReader for database reads. Configure appropriate page size (typically 500). Use @StepScope for parameter injection. Implement proper null handling and data validation. Support multiple date formats when applicable. IMPORTANT: If reader exceeds 150 lines, apply refactoring rules: extract date parsing to helper class, extract query building to helper class, extract RowMapper to separate mapper class.
componentDesign.processor: Keep processors focused on transformation logic. Use @StepScope for parameter injection. Inject enrichment services when needed. Return error status records instead of failing the entire batch. Map domain entities to DTOs with proper business logic.
componentDesign.writer: Use ItemWriter with batch operations. Handle individual write failures gracefully. Log errors with context but throw custom exceptions. Use repository pattern for persistence.
componentDesign.step: Configure steps with: chunk-based processing, transaction manager, fault tolerance with skip limits, task executor for parallel processing, skip listeners for error tracking. Use @JobScope for step beans.

jobConfiguration.structure: Job configuration should: use @Configuration and @RequiredArgsConstructor, inject exception handler, use JobBuilder with job name, register exception handler as listener, reference step beans with @Qualifier.
jobConfiguration.naming: Use consistent naming: {Domain}JobBean for job beans, {Domain}StepBean for step beans, {Domain}Job for job names. Follow the pattern throughout the application.
jobConfiguration.documentation: Document job purpose, parameters required, processing workflow, and references to related components with comprehensive JavaDoc.

logging.strategy: Use @Slf4j consistently. Log entry/exit points at INFO level. Log errors with context at ERROR level. Include correlation IDs (batchId, solicitud numbers). Use consistent log prefixes like [JOB-NAME].
logging.avoidVerbosity: Remove debugging logs before production. Avoid logging every processed item. Log summaries and statistics instead. Log only actionable information.

constants.organization: Create dedicated Constants class for each batch job. Organize constants by category: table names, column names, SQL clauses, log messages, configuration values, status codes. Use descriptive constant names.
constants.usage: Reference constants instead of string literals. Keep SQL fragments as constants. Maintain log message templates as constants for consistency.

testing.approach: Write unit tests for processors with mock dependencies. Write integration tests for readers and writers using Testcontainers. Test skip scenarios and exception handling. Verify step and job configuration.

bddAnnotations.description: ALL test methods MUST include BDD (Behavior-Driven Development) annotations in JavaDoc format. This is MANDATORY and part of the Definition of Done.

structure.Feature: The general feature or capability being tested
structure.Scenario: The specific scenario of the test case
structure.Then: Expected results (can be multiple bullet points)

bddAnnotations.format:
/**
 * Feature: [Feature name]
 * Scenario: [Specific scenario]
 *
 * Given: [Preconditions]
 * When: [Action]
 * Then:
 *  - [Expected result 1]
 *  - [Expected result 2]
 *  - [Expected result N]
 */
benefits: Living documentation - tests serve as executable specifications
Traceability - direct connection between business requirements and test code
Maintainability - easier to update and understand tests over time
Communication - common language between developers, QA, and stakeholders
Onboarding - accelerates understanding for new team members

sections: // Arrange (Given) - Setup test context and preconditions
// Act (When) - Execute the action being tested
testStructure.naming: Use descriptive method names following: methodName_Condition_ExpectedResult

testGrouping.description: Organize and group related tests using JUnit 5 features for better structure and execution control

suiteClasses.purpose: Group multiple test classes together for organized execution
suiteClasses.usage: Create a test suite class to execute related test classes as a single unit
benefits: Execute related tests together in CI/CD pipelines
Organize test results by functional area
Useful for Sonar and coverage reports

assertAllGrouping.purpose: Group multiple related assertions so all execute even if one fails
assertAllGrouping.usage: Use when validating multiple properties of the same object or related conditions
benefits: See all assertion failures at once instead of stopping at first failure
Better error reporting for complex validations
Logical grouping of related checks

dataGroupingValidation.purpose: Validate that code correctly groups or aggregates data
dataGroupingValidation.usage: Use in tests to verify batch processing logic that groups results by key
benefits: Validates grouping/aggregation logic in batch processors
Tests real-world data transformation scenarios
Useful for validating summary calculations

nestedTests.purpose: Organize related test scenarios within a single test class
nestedTests.usage: Group tests by scenario or context using nested test classes
benefits: Better test organization within large test classes
Shared setup for related tests with @BeforeEach in nested class
Improved test report readability

guidelines: Use @Suite to group test classes by functional area (Reader, Processor, Writer)
Use assertAll() for validating multiple properties of same object
Use Collectors.groupingBy() in tests to validate aggregation logic
Use @Nested for organizing related test scenarios within a class
Keep test suites focused on a single component or feature
Document the purpose of test suites and nested classes

readerRefactoring.trigger: When a Reader class exceeds 150-200 lines
readerRefactoring.strategy: Extract responsibilities into dedicated helper and mapper classes following Single Responsibility Principle

dateParsingLogic.description: Pure date parsing and formatting logic without dependencies. Support multiple date formats. Include validation and error handling.
dateParsingLogic.example: ChecksDateParser - handles parsing process dates in multiple formats (dd-MM-yyyy, yyyy-MM-dd)

queryBuildingLogic.type: Utility class with static factory methods
queryBuildingLogic.description: Encapsulates SQL query construction logic. Build SELECT, FROM, WHERE clauses separately. Return configured PagingQueryProvider.
queryBuildingLogic.example: ChecksQueryProvider - creates PostgresPagingQueryProvider with all query clauses

rowMappingLogic.description: Extract inner RowMapper class to dedicated file. Organize mapping in logical sections (basic info, batch info, detail info, calculated fields). Use private helper methods for null-safe field mapping with functional interfaces.
rowMappingLogic.example: CheckRowMapper - maps ResultSet to Check entity with organized sections and error handling

benefits: Reader class reduced to ~100-120 lines (core reading logic only)
Helper classes can be tested independently
Mapper classes can be reused if needed
Easier to maintain and understand
Better adherence to Single Responsibility Principle
Improved code organization and discoverability
implementation: Create reader/helper/ subdirectory for helper classes
Create reader/mapper/ subdirectory for mapper classes
Extract date parsing to *DateParser helper with static methods
Update Reader to use the new helper and mapper classes
Maintain comprehensive JavaDoc in all classes

parallelProcessing.taskExecutor: Configure dedicated TaskExecutor for each batch with: appropriate core/max pool sizes, queue capacity, thread name prefix, graceful shutdown settings. Comment out if reader implements ItemStream to avoid warnings.
parallelProcessing.chunkSize: Configure chunk size based on: data volume, transaction size, memory constraints. Typical values: 500-1000 for normal loads, 100-200 for heavy processing.
